title: NPV vs IRR
description: Compare NPV and IRR to understand which investment metric to use.
intro: NPV and IRR are both capital-budgeting tools. NPV tells you the dollar value an investment adds, while IRR tells you the percentage return. They often agree, but NPV is generally more reliable.

comparisonTable.functionB: Internal rate of return as a percentage
Accept if IRR > required rate of return
Assumes cash flows reinvest at the IRR
Can produce multiple solutions for alternating cash flows

whenToUseA: Use NPV when you need a dollar-value measure of value creation and you have a reliable discount rate.
whenToUseB: Use IRR when communicating the percentage return of an investment or comparing projects of different sizes.
verdict: NPV is generally preferred for decision-making because it directly measures value added and avoids the multiple-IRR problem.

faq.question: Can NPV and IRR conflict?
faq.answer: Yes, with non-conventional cash flows or mutually exclusive projects of different scales.

faq.question: Which is better for ranking projects?
faq.answer: NPV is better for ranking because it reflects absolute value creation.
